This relationship can be represented by the equation \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"K equals, one half m v squared\">\x3C/span>, where \x3Cspan>K\x3C/span> is the kinetic energy, \x3Cspan>m \x3C/span>is the mass, and \x3Cspan>v \x3C/span>is the speed. Substituting a mass of 4 kilograms for \x3Cspan>m \x3C/span>and a kinetic energy of 18 joules for \x3Cspan>K \x3C/span>results in the equation \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"18 equals, one half times 4, times v squared\">\x3C/span>, or \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"18 equals, 2 v squared\">\x3C/span>. Dividing both sides of this equation by 2 yields \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"9 equals, v squared\">\x3C/span>. Taking the square root of both sides yields \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"v equals, negative 3\">\x3C/span> and \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"v equals 3\">\x3C/span>. Since speed can&rsquo;t be expressed as a negative number, the speed of the object is 3 meters per second.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>Choice B is incorrect and may result from computation errors.
